$comment: Names and ids only, never a secret. The crew addresses Airtable by NAME and
resolves each name to your base's ids at startup, so a duplicated base needs
only a new airtable.baseId. Change a name only if your base renames the field.

board.$note: Who holds the board. airtable = the real base, credentials from ~/.claude/productive-crew/credentials.json or the AIRTABLE_API_KEY environment variable (never a file in the repo). file = .crew/board.json, for running the crew with no account at all — fixtures, tests, a first component before a base exists. It is a different board, not a cache of one: a cached copy would go stale and still look live.

airtable.$comment: Table and column names are Title Case, matching the base exactly. Airtable resolves table names case-sensitively.

choices.$comment: Cell VALUES, not column names. The Development formula and scripts/status.js both match the re-test result on the substring "re-test" rather than the whole label, so renaming that option does not silently break the ladder.

figma.$note: Only tokens is required. One Figma file? set tokens, leave components blank. Components are read per-row from Airtable, so add component files only if you want them named here.

stack.$note: Set at /productive-crew:setup. Decides the component code AND the token output. Regenerates tools.md.

repo.$note: Branch names are yours. Defaults below. If your repo already uses develop/master or another flow, /productive-crew:setup detects it and maps the three tiers (work → preview → production) to your branches. If you rename these, also update the branch refs in .github/workflows/pages.yml.

tokenBuilder.$note: The build runs when tokens/tokens.json changes. The schedule is a safety net for when a change lands without triggering a run — not the primary trigger.

schedule.$note: What you INTENDED to run on a clock, in hours. The plugin cannot schedule anything — it ships hooks, which fire on events, not on the clock — so the job itself lives outside (a Claude Code scheduled task, launchd, cron, CI). Declaring it here is what lets the crew notice when it stops happening: scripts/run-log.js compares this against .crew/runs/<kind>.jsonl and the session-start hook says so out loud. Remove a key to stop checking it — an undeclared cadence is never warned about.

deploy.$note: enabled=false is NOT WIRED YET: no staging link, so no QA stage and no Staging Testing rows. provider decides WHO publishes the staging build — the crew only needs a URL it can verify, and it does not care who produced it.
deploy.$providerNote: Only two values: github-pages = the bundled .github/workflows/pages.yml builds and publishes on push. command = you publish, via stagingCommand/productionCommand below. A host name is NOT a value — Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare and the rest are all 'command' plus their CLI. The contract for a command is exactly one thing: print the deployed URL as the LAST line of stdout. The Engineer captures that line, verifies it answers 200, and reports it. Absent = github-pages.
deploy.stagingCommand: npm run tokens:build && npm run build-storybook && npx vercel deploy storybook-static --yes
deploy.productionCommand: npm run tokens:build && npm run build-storybook && npx vercel deploy storybook-static --prod --yes
